strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN with TCP-shaped FakeTCP outer packets, UDP/datagram-like inner behavior, DTLS 1.3, and a compact WBD-owned FEC layer suited to OpenWrt/Linux/Windows owned endpoints.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: Replace the resource-heavy generic UDPspeeder process with a narrow WBD-owned FEC candidate, using UDPspeeder 20:20 as the oracle baseline and correcting the steady-state 200-Mbit sizing methodology.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not broaden the matrix. First implement one fixed 20+20 systematic erasure-code path with bounded buffers, then A/B only high-information 200-Mbit public-link points. Keep UDPspeeder until the candidate is at least as good on delivery/tail latency and materially better on RSS/CPU.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Focused workflow transport-200m run 32819141473 completed successfully: prepare, RTT 20/100/300/600 bench jobs and aggregate all passed, producing 20 rows for symmetric loss 0/1/5/10/20%. Public veth capacity was 200 Mbit/s per direction and inner offered load was 90 Mbit/s with UDPspeeder mode0 20:20, DTLS 1.3 and FakeTCP. The request/echo generator makes this a 90-Mbit/s full-duplex inner stress. At 20 ms / 0% loss the stack returned 39.217 Mbit/s within the accounting window, delivery ratio 0.4357, p99 282.5 ms, with zero qdisc loss; this is strong evidence of CPU/queueing pressure rather than network-loss recovery. Aggregate RSS was 28,976 KiB: UDPspeeder 21,096 KiB, DTLS 5,624 KiB, udp2raw 2,256 KiB. Process CPU deltas over the case were UDPspeeder ~2.67 s, DTLS ~2.70 s and udp2raw ~2.29 s across both endpoints, showing CPU pressure is distributed while UDPspeeder clearly dominates memory (~73% of userspace RSS). Across all 20 cases total RSS stayed roughly 28.3-30.5 MiB, so no RTT/loss memory blow-up appeared. The run also revealed a measurement defect: the post-send drain timeout grows with RTT, responses during drain count toward delivery while throughput keeps a 2-s denominator, and CPU deltas include drain while cpu_core_fraction divides by 2 s. Therefore higher-RTT delivery/throughput/core-fraction values are not valid for quantitative cross-RTT comparison. This limitation and the valid capacity/RSS conclusions are persisted in docs/benchmarks/v2-200m-first-pass.md at 9ba1ca8cee6d2d6a865b4ae96413c556a708c951. The temporary [200m] PR title flag has been removed.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Build a minimal WBD-owned FEC v0 and A/B it against UDPspeeder 20:20. Preferred first codec is fixed systematic 20 data + 20 parity Reed-Solomon-style erasure coding with preallocated bounded block buffers, original packet-length metadata and a small flush timer. In parallel, correct the 200-Mbit sizing probe to separate one-way bulk throughput/CPU from a low-rate latency probe and to use actual measurement wall time.
continuation_cursor.why_now: The 200-Mbit pass shows UDPspeeder consumes about three quarters of current userspace RSS, while the project only needs one narrow fixed FEC behavior. Eliminating the generic UDPspeeder process can remove a large memory allocation and one UDP process/socket hop per side. A naive single-XOR parity scheme is too weak for the desired 20:20 loss protection, so the simplification should be protocol/implementation scope, not a weaker erasure model by accident.
continuation_cursor.done_when: A WBD-owned FEC candidate can encode/decode fixed 20+20 blocks, handle variable original packet lengths without stream semantics, bound memory explicitly, flush partial blocks on a small timer, pass deterministic loss/reorder unit tests, and run the corrected focused 200-Mbit A/B against the pinned UDPspeeder oracle. Report per-endpoint RSS, codec CPU, end-to-end CPU, one-way delivery/goodput and separate latency under a small set of RTT/loss points.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: Add a minimal internal FEC package and benchmark: systematic 20+20 shards, GF(256) Reed-Solomon via a thin replaceable codec interface, bounded buffer pool and block header. Unit-test recovery for 0..20 missing shards and rejection beyond parity budget. Do not remove UDPspeeder from the product baseline until the A/B passes.
